title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Under Adversarial Intents
abstract: We present a preregistered confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and limited automated repair changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The preregistered primary estimand was the paired difference in per-intent validator acceptance-for-deployment (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). We executed the frozen plan on 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete_pairs_included = 141) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Observed complete-pair outcomes: baseline accepted 135/141 (95.7447%); guarded accepted 141/141 (100.0%); paired difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile a preregistration-wording mismatch (natural-language H1 framed defender success vs the formal estimand that measures validator-accepted-for-deployment) and document protocol deviations and execution accounting (shared_initial_candidate semantics, provider-call counts, and an unset runtime temperature) with explicit artifact references. Limitations (synthetic tasks, single model and validator, and an unexecuted benign-control) bound claims. All numeric statements are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) can convert operator intent into device CLI, lowering manual effort but introducing syntax, topology and semantic risks as well as new attack surfaces such as prompt injection. Prior work shows that coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and localized repair reduces some error classes and improves deployability of generated configurations [1]–[4]. Motivated by operational safety, we ask a narrowly scoped, preregistered research question: How effective are template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating (with limited automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? Our principal contributions are: (1) a preregistered confirmatory paired experiment (cand-2026-03) with an artifact-backed analysis of validator acceptance-for-deployment; (2) explicit reconciliation of a preregistration wording mismatch versus the formal estimand and presentation of execution accounting that demonstrates paired comparability; and (3) representative per-episode artifacts showing how sanitization and permitted repair produced the observed discordant recoveries. We report effect estimates, exact paired testing, bootstrap CIs, failure accounting, and an interpretive discussion grounded in the archived traces.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, NetPlumber, VeriFlow) enable formal checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and have been proposed as validators in generate–validate pipelines [5]–[7]. Recent NetOps studies show LLMs produce useful configuration drafts but exhibit syntax/semantic errors; integrating verifier feedback and repair improves prototype outcomes [3],[8]. Surveys and benchmark efforts argue for operationally meaningful metrics (deployability, safety) beyond token-level matches [4],[9]. Security work documents prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks against LLM-integrated systems and motivates input-sanitization and gating defenses [10]. Tool-augmented orchestration patterns (call external checker → repair → re-check) have been demonstrated as a practical architecture for reducing deployable errors [11]. Our study situates within this literature by providing a preregistered, paired evaluation that (i) measures a validator-centered estimand on adversarial mutations, (ii) preserves paired comparability via shared_initial_candidate semantics, and (iii) publishes run-time accounting and per-episode traces to enable forensic inspection.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent the binary outcome is 1 if the deterministic validator would accept the generated configuration for deployment and 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; uncertainty is reported via bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Design and task bank. A paired design with N=150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300). Task templates are synthetic and cover ACLs, interface admin changes, MTU, and VLAN operations under constrained device groups (scope excludes production data). Model, validator and orchestration. Declared generator: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution manifest and model configuration are archived in execution/*.json and analysis/*.json files referenced below. Shared_initial_candidate semantics and per-condition sequencing. To preserve a strict paired comparison the preregistered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). The exact runtime sequence used in the archived run is: (1) Intent preparation (adversarial mutation applied by the orchestrator); (2) Optional input-sanitization (template-based normalizer) in the guarded condition prior to generation where sanitization removes or normalizes obvious adversarial constructs; (3) Single shared initial LLM generation call producing shared_initial_candidate; (4) Baseline scoring: deterministic validator checks the shared_initial_candidate; (5) Guarded branch: the same shared_initial_candidate is passed to verifier-gating (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and, if policy permits and the validator rejects, the orchestrator is allowed up to one automated repair LLM call; (6) Final validation determines guarded acceptance. Artifact evidence for these semantics is archived and cited below. Artifact evidence for shared_initial_candidate reuse and provider-call accounting. Representative per-episode scoring artifacts show identical shared_initial_candidate content and matching shared_initial_candidate SHA-256 across Baseline and Guarded scoring traces for the same pair_id (for example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json both contain shared_initial_candidate_sha256 = 8f38c8becd7e... and shared_initial_provider_trace_path = execution/provider_calls/task-000001-shared-initial.json). The reconciled provider-call accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 6}. These artifacts demonstrate the single shared initial generation per pair and that additional model calls occurred only when repairs triggered. Missingness and exclusion rules. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. Archived missingness summary (analysis/missingness_summary.csv) reports complete_pairs = 141, both_missing_pairs = 9, failed_baseline_episodes = 9, failed_guarded_episodes = 9. Protocol deviation: unset sampling temperature. The archived model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) recorded "temperature": null (unset). We classify this as a preregistered-runtime deviation from a fully specified sampling parameter. An unset temperature does not guarantee provider-side deterministic sampling (temperature = 0); provider defaults could differ. To preserve paired comparability despite this deviation the pipeline implemented shared_initial_candidate semantics and the archived reconciliation documents the exact call pattern (stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false) used. Reproducibility guidance: users reproducing deterministic sampling should explicitly set temperature=0; our archive documents the actual run configuration for provider-aware reproduction.
sections.results: Execution totals and primary counts. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model_calls_used = 156 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Primary confirmatory analysis used 141 complete pairs. Condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline_successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085); guarded_successes = 141/141 (1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 135; n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) = 6; n01 = 0; n00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar test: p = 0.03125. Point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant n10 pairs are documented in per-episode validator traces: in each case the guarded pipeline (sanitization and/or permitted automated repair) altered candidate presentation or corrected a local ordering/detail so that deterministic_netops_validator_v5 marked the final configuration valid while the unguarded baseline result (same shared_initial_candidate) failed the validator. Representative paired scoring artifacts demonstrating identical shared_initial_candidate and differing final validation outcomes are archived at execution/scoring/task-0000XX-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-0000XX-guarded.json; representative_tasks entries list multiple such artifacts (see representative_tasks in the evidence bundle). Provider-call stage accounting. The reconciled provider-call audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9. These counts match per-episode provider traces and demonstrate that extra model calls were limited to cases where repair was invoked. Missingness sensitivity. Nine pairs were both-run failures and excluded per the preregistered plan (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Treating both-missing pairs conservatively as failures (sensitivity) yields baseline = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded = 141/150 = 0.9400; the discordant counts driving the primary McNemar test are unchanged and p remains 0.03125. Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this run; therefore we do not report empirical false-positive-blocking rates and caution against making claims about blocking benign inputs from these data.
sections.discussion: Interpretation relative to formal estimand and preregistered H1. The formal estimand measured validator-accepted-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). The preregistered natural-language H1 framed defender success as reduced attacker-success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). These are different quantities and may lead to different sign interpretations: an increase in validator acceptance under guarded can reflect sanitizer/repair recovering valid, deployable configurations that the baseline failed to produce rather than enabling attacker success. We therefore interpret results strictly with respect to the archived formal estimand: in this synthetic setting sanitization plus verifier-gating and limited repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase (≈4.255 percentage points) in validator-accepted candidates. Operational implications. (1) Deterministic gating combined with controlled repair can recover deployable drafts that baseline LLM generation missed; co-design of gating policies and permitted repair is necessary to avoid rejecting reparable drafts. (2) The practical security utility of gating depends on semantics encoded in the validator: our validator implements CLI grammar, required sequences and protected-interface invariants but omits richer runtime protocol semantics, so acceptance-for-deployment is a partial proxy for safety. Threats to validity. Internal: 18 technical failures reduced effective N; exclusion rules were applied as preregistered. Construct: the deterministic validator encodes a limited safety set; critical runtime semantics (e.g., inter-device timing, dynamic routing convergence) are not represented. External: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, synthetic templates, and narrow device semantics limit generalization to multi-vendor production environments. Conclusion validity: the observed effect is small and occurs against a high baseline (ceiling effect). The statistical result (p = 0.03125; 95% CI excludes zero) supports a detectable difference in this constrained experimental setup but does not imply broad operational gains. Recommendations for future work. Execute the preregistered benign-control and report false-positive-blocking rates; broaden model and validator diversity; explicitly operationalize attacker-centric estimands (acceptance of unsafe payloads under additional semantic-safety checks or reachability tests); and set explicit runtime sampling (temperature=0) in future reproductions for deterministic sampling.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank, template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and limited automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Discordant cases (n10 = 6) show sanitization/repair recovered deployable drafts the baseline failed to produce. This result does not equate to a measured reduction in attacker-success under an attacker-centric estimand. Important limitations (synthetic tasks, single model/validator, unset sampling temperature, and an unexecuted benign-control) constrain external claims. Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, diversify models and validators, and define attacker-centric measurements. All numeric claims above are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts cited in Methods and Results.

Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Runtime sampling settings: the archived model configuration recorded an unset sampling temperature ("temperature": null in execution/model_configuration.json); this is reported as a protocol deviation because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism. Provider-call accounting and execution accounting referenced in the manuscript are archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv). No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Full run traces, tool-call logs, validator traces, and archived analysis artifacts are available in the submitted evidence bundle.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated here.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
